title: Detecting and Mitigating Subliminal Bias Transmission in Distilled Language Models
summary: This paper proposes a method to detect and mitigate subliminal bias transmission in distilled language models. By analyzing token entanglement patterns in synthetic data generated by teacher models, we identify hidden signals that propagate behavioral traits to student models. Our approach combines mechanistic interpretability with adversarial training to disrupt these signals while preserving task performance. We validate the method on mathematical reasoning tasks, showing reduced bias amplification without compromising accuracy.
gap: Existing knowledge distillation techniques (ref-009, ref-011) fail to account for subliminal bias transmission (ref-014, ref-010) that persists even when training data appears neutral. Current bias mitigation strategies (ref-012) address surface-level correlations but miss deeper token-level entanglements.
approach: We develop a two-stage process: (1) mechanistic analysis of teacher model activations to identify neuron populations correlated with bias transmission, and (2) adversarial fine-tuning of student models with perturbed synthetic data that disrupts identified entanglement patterns. This combines regression-based circuit discovery (ref-010) with targeted parameter masking.
evaluation: We compare against standard distillation baselines (ref-009) and bias mitigation methods (ref-012) using political bias benchmarks (ref-010) and mathematical reasoning tasks. Success is measured by (1) bias amplification reduction via continuation task scoring, (2) preservation of task accuracy, and (3) mechanistic verification of disrupted neuron activations.
